newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Motorola pulls out of Ukraine mobile market.
newsitem.headline: Motorola pulls out of Ukraine mobile market.

text.p: Motorola Inc has pulled out of the cellular phone market in the former Soviet republic of Ukraine, Interfax-Ukraine news agency quoted a public affairs spokesman for the U.S. telecoms giant as saying.
Motorola officials were not immediately available to comment on the report.
Interfax-Ukraine said Motorola was "stopping its investment activity" on Ukraine's mobile phones market in connection with "constantly changing conditions" of activities and licensing.
Motorola's Ukrainian partner was one of three companies to win the right to launch a GSM 900 standard network at a tender earlier this month.
Interfax-Ukraine quoted Motorola's public affairs department as saying it would continue its other activities in Ukraine.
A Motorola official said last year that Motorola was intending to invest $120 million in the nationwide system.
Foreign investors in Ukraine, particularly in the nascent telecoms sector, have complained about bureaucratic hurdles, demands for bribes and a lack of legislation in the past.
